name: xAI

summary.text: xAI is the artificial intelligence company that builds the Grok models and operates the Colossus data centers in Memphis. It was organized as X.AI Holdings Corp. and its Series B, C and E financings were announced by the company or disclosed in SpaceX's 2026 registration statement. SpaceX acquired X.AI Holdings Corp. in a share exchange effective February 2, 2026 (the 'xAI Merger'). SpaceX's filings state that Elon Musk controls SpaceX.

sources.publisher: SEC EDGAR (SpaceX, Space Exploration Technologies Corp.)
sources.title: Form S-1/A Amendment No. 2

facts.claim: SpaceX acquired X.AI Holdings Corp. effective February 2, 2026 in what SpaceX's filing calls the 'xAI Merger'; each outstanding xAI common share converted into 0.1433 SpaceX shares.
facts.quote: X.AI Holdings Corp., which was acquired by SpaceX, effective February 2, 2026 (the "xAI Merger")

facts.claim: SpaceX's registration statement defines 'xAI' as X.AI Holdings LLC or, before the xAI Merger, X.AI Holdings Corp., together with its subsidiaries.
facts.quote: "xAI" refers to X.AI Holdings LLC or, prior to the xAI Merger, X.AI Holdings Corp., together with its subsidiaries, as applicable.

facts.claim: SpaceX's registration statement says Elon Musk will hold about 82.4% of SpaceX's voting power after its IPO; SpaceX now owns xAI following the merger. The filing does not state Musk's personal stake in xAI.
facts.quote: Mr. Musk will hold approximately 82.4% of the voting power of our common stock

facts.claim: Under the xAI Merger, SpaceX's registration statement says xAI's Series E preferred purchase by Tesla ($2,000 million, agreed January 2026) was converted into a right to acquire SpaceX Class A common stock.
facts.quote: In January 2026, Tesla entered into an agreement with xAI to invest $2,000 million via a purchase of xAI Series E Redeemable Convertible Preferred Stock.

facts.claim: SpaceX's registration statement reports carrying values for xAI redeemable convertible preferred stock of $7,001 million for Series B and $6,000 million for Series C (not the announced round sizes).

Subsidiaries of xAI lease computing equipment from Valor under agreements with aggregate cash payments of $6,986 million, $6,633 million and $6,587 million over the lives of the leases; xAI subsidiaries paid $885 million under them in 2025.
facts.quote: Pursuant to the lease agreements described above, our subsidiaries have made payments of $885 million in 2025

facts.claim: Antonio J. Gracias, a member of SpaceX's board, is founder, CEO and Chief Investment Officer of Valor Equity Partners.
facts.quote: Mr. Antonio J. Gracias, a member of our board, also serves as the founder, CEO and Chief Investment Officer of Valor Equity Partners

facts.claim: SEC Form D filed by X.AI Holdings Corp. (Nevada) on January 6, 2026 lists Elon Musk and Jared Birchall as related persons, with total offering amount $19,999,999,972, amount sold $16,599,961,030 and 131 investors already invested.
SEC Form D filed by X.AI Holdings Corp. (Nevada) on August 6, 2025 records $5,318,549,402 sold and 7 investors already invested.

xAI announced that it had closed a $6 billion Series C round, with participation from investors including A16Z, Blackrock, Fidelity, Kingdom Holdings, Lightspeed, MGX, Morgan Stanley, OIA, QIA, Sequoia Capital, Valor Equity Partners and Vy Capital.
facts.quote: We have closed our Series C funding round of $6 billion with participation from key investors including A16Z, Blackrock, Fidelity Management & Research Company, Kingdom Holdings, Lightspeed, MGX, Morgan Stanley, OIA, QIA, Sequoia Capital, Valor Equity Partners and Vy Capital, amongst others.

facts.claim: NVIDIA and AMD participated as strategic investors in xAI's Series C round.
facts.quote: Strategic investors NVIDIA and AMD also participated and continue to support xAI in rapidly scaling our infrastructure.

facts.claim: xAI and Saudi Arabia's HUMAIN, which is backed by the Public Investment Fund, announced in November 2025 a 500MW data center in Saudi Arabia, with Grok to be deployed in the Kingdom.
facts.quote: Elon Musk’s xAI is partnering with Humain to build a 500MW data center in Saudi Arabia.

sources.title: xAI and Humain to build 500MW Saudi Arabia data center

facts.claim: Daniel Rowland is listed as overseeing xAI's data center operations, including the Memphis facility.
facts.quote: Daniel Rowland oversees X.AI Corp.’s massive data center operations, including management of the Memphis facility—the world’s largest supercomputer comprising over 200,000 GPUs.

sources.title: X.AI Corp Leadership and Executive Team

facts.claim: CB Insights lists Elon Musk as xAI's Founder and Chief Executive Officer.
facts.quote: xAI's current Founder, Chief Executive Officer is Elon Reeve Musk .

openQuestions: Formation date: SpaceX's S-1/A states the xAI entity was acquired effective February 2, 2026, but does not give a formation date. The Nevada Secretary of State record was not reachable (Bizapedia returned a human-verification wall), so no formation date is recorded. Wikipedia's SpaceXAI article gives 2023-03-09 with a note that the announcement was July 12, 2023; that page is not a valid citation and was not used.

Musk's direct ownership stake in xAI: the S-1/A states Musk controls SpaceX (about 82.4% voting power post-IPO), and SpaceX owns xAI after the merger; the S-1/A does not state Musk's personal percentage in xAI itself. Not recorded as a direct ownership link.

Series B and C amounts ($6 billion each) and their named investors come from xAI's own Series C post and from Houdao (a secondary site for Series B). No Form D for the Series B round was retrievable: the X.AI Corp. Form D documents return 403 or 404 on SEC Archives, and the EDGAR index pages list filings without opening them.

Series E: only Tesla ($2,000 million) is confirmed as a named Series E investor from the S-1/A. The $20 billion Series E total, the Nvidia and Cisco participation, and the MGX, QIA and HUMAIN ($3 billion) participation come from Revenue Memo only and are unconfirmed.
The June 2025 $5 billion debt package, the July 2025 SpaceX $2 billion equity investment, and the March 2026 $20 billion bridge loan are reported by Revenue Memo only and are not recorded.

Federal procurement: USAspending.gov is a JavaScript application. The browser rendered an empty search page for 'X.AI Corp' with no results list, and its API returned 405 for GET. This is an inconclusive result, not a finding of no awards.
Lobbying: the Senate LDA filings API returned zero results for client names 'xAI' and 'X.AI Corp' (count 0). Recorded as a negative search result for the API only.

Political spending: the FEC committee search (api.open.fec.gov, committees 'xAI' and 'X.AI') returned zero committees. The FEC candidate-name search returned unrelated results. Recorded as a negative search result for those queries only.

Litigation: CourtListener's search API lists federal complaints naming X.AI Corp. in 2026 (for example Jane Doe 1 v. X.AI Corp., N.D. Cal. 5:26-cv-09617; Neural AI, LLC v. X.AI Corp., W.D. Tex. 7:26-cv-00319). Docket pages returned 403, so these are recorded only as search listings, not as recorded findings.

Executive roles other than Musk's come from aggregator pages (Exa, CB Insights) and are not corroborated. No xAI board seats were confirmed. Jared Birchall signed the 2025 and 2026 Form Ds as Corporate Secretary; his Neuralink role is not recorded as a connection.
No fetched source established corporate links to Neuralink, Google, Meta, SoftBank, OpenAI, Uber or Amazon, so none are recorded.
Clipped to the Trove: the SpaceX S-1/A, the X.AI Holdings Form D (2026), and the USAspending results page.
